Thanks for taking my intro at KubeCon last week. VectorForge is evaluating a private-label runtime option where we bundle an inference runtime (licensed/embedded) into our analytics appliance. We liked Redwood's performance profile and are exploring an RMS-style reseller agreement (we ship under our brand, you provide the engine/updates).

Quick list of items my legal and engineering teams want clarity on so we can scope an MOU:
- Certification process: what steps are required for a partner to get an approved ‘Redwood Labelled Runtime’ certification?
- Branding and disclosure: allowed co-branding, customer-facing attribution wording, and whether we can remove Redwood logos entirely under certain tiers.
- Security/audit: requirements for SOC/SaaS telemetry, which telemetry is mandatory versus optional, and expectations around data flow.
- Update cadence & signed binaries: how are security patches delivered (signed artifacts, hotfix windows)?
- Support & SLA: breakouts for P1/P2/P3 and whether 24x7 support is available for certified resellers.
- Pricing: commercial model for embedded licensing (per-seat, per-instance, committed throughput).

Alex —

Really appreciate the clear list and the outline — this is exactly the level of detail that helps speed reviews. Short answers here, and I can schedule a joint technical + legal sync once we align on a few baseline choices:

- Certification: we run a two-track certification: technical (security, integration, packaging) and commercial (SLA, revenue share, branding). Technical includes a checklist, pentest submission or SOC report, and one integration smoke test. Commercial requires an MOU and a partner technical addendum. See attached: Redwood_Cert_Guide_v2.docx — it has the checklist and lead times.
- Branding: we support three tiers: Co-branded (Redwood + partner), White-label (Redwood name removed but partner displays ‘Powered by Redwood’ in partner-only docs), and Private-label (no external attribution but requires higher annual contract and security attestation). The Private-label path requires code signing and quarterly attestations.
- Security/telemetry: mandatory telemetry is limited to error/health metrics and kernel versioning (we do not ship model prompts back by default). Any additional telemetry requires written consent in the MOU and data-processing addendum.
- Updates & signed binaries: certified partners receive signed releases via our partner artifact registry. Hotfix windows are agreed in the MOU; critical security updates are prioritized and flagged.
- Support & SLA: we offer an enhanced partner SLA for certified resellers (SLA add-on) with options for 24x7 for P1s. On-call rotations and escalation channels are part of the commercial package.
- Pricing: we have a baseline embedded license (per-instance with volume discounts) and an alternative committed throughput model for appliances. Karthik, Vanessa — can you prepare a preliminary pricing band for VectorForge after the tech call?

If that aligns, propose Wed 2026-12-15 10:00 PT for a kickoff. Emily — does that work?

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart

Alex / team —

Thanks for the outline — a few technical clarifications from our side ahead of the call:

1) Private-label packaging: we can provide a containerized runtime, signed artifacts, and an optional installer. For on-prem appliances, we require a minimal heartbeat to our partner registry for licensing validation; offline/air-gapped installs are supported but require an annual offline attestation process.

2) Telemetry: default is health/errors/kernel metrics only. If you want usage telemetry (token counts, prompt lengths), we need explicit DSP and potential MCAs.

3) Model updates: models are separate from the runtime — customers can pin model versions. Partners that want model updates included in the embedded product buy a model-inclusion license (adds to cost).

4) Certification test: we run an integration smoke test (30–90 minutes) in a mirror appliance environment. Passing criteria: successful startup, kernel init, KV cache validation, and upgrade path verification.

Next steps I suggest for the tech call: share a small test image (or provide credentials to a lab appliance), confirm whether air-gapped mode is required, and list which bundles (runtime-only vs runtime+models) you expect to ship.

Forwarding: please see attached internal guidelines we reference for partner packaging.

—Vanessa
Partner Engineering Manager — Redwood Inference
